body: Decomposing the moves [approximate, my arithmetic from public EPS/P/E ranges]: Apple 2003-12 ~110x was ~100% EPS with P/E compression; Apple 2016-23 ~8x was ~half EPS (x2.9, buyback-aided) and half P/E (11x -> 30x); Microsoft 2014-25 ~15x = EPS ~5x x P/E ~2.5x; Costco 2009-26 ~29x = EPS ~7x x P/E ~3.5x; Meta 2022-25 ~9x = EPS ~2.8x x P/E ~3x; Palantir 2022-25 ~35x was mostly multiple (P/S 8.5x -> 137x vs revenue ~2.5x); Tesla 2019-21 ~35x was mostly multiple. Durability followed the mix: EPS-led winners kept compounding or stalled gently; multiple-led winners gave back 36-73% (Palantir, Tesla, Celsius, Enphase) even while still growing. The best risk/reward combos had both engines starting from a depressed multiple (the twin-engine pattern: Apple 2016 at ~10x, Meta 2022 at ~9x, Microsoft 2014 at ~14x). Lesson: estimate what share of the expected return requires the multiple to rise; above ~50% from an already-high multiple, the position is a bet on sentiment and should be sized as such.
title: EPS growth vs P/E rerating: which engine drove the multiple decides durability

body: Deep-dive protocol v1.4 says value non-operating stakes separately when they exceed 20% of market cap. The threshold was chosen by the drafting agent, not derived from any lesson or test. Treat as provisional; revisit after 3+ holdco dives.
title: Holdco stake >20% of market cap trigger is an untested rule of thumb
